plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a standard alternating high/low index dielectric stack can achieve dual-band transmission in the mid-IR with suppression of adjacent thermal background bands. The design draws from recalled knowledge of quarter-wave stack principles adapted for dual-passband operation. I would have wanted to look up measured dispersion data for ZnS and MgF2 specifically in the 3.5-5.5 μm range to confirm transparency and index contrast, and to verify CaF2 substrate compatibility with these materials at deposition temperatures.

routes.title: ZnS-MgF2 Alternating Dual-Band IR Filter on Daimon-20
routes.scientific_hypothesis: An alternating high-low index dielectric stack with optimized individual layer thicknesses can produce two distinct transmission bands at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm while suppressing transmission at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm, using only conventional IR-transparent materials.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory: alternating layers of high and low refractive index create constructive interference in passbands and destructive interference in stopbands. For dual-band operation, the layer thicknesses must be tuned so that multiple harmonic orders of the stack align with both target wavelengths. ZnS provides high index (~2.2-2.4 in mid-IR), MgF2 provides low index (~1.3-1.4 in mid-IR), giving sufficient index contrast for effective filtering.
routes.proposed_topology: 22-layer alternating stack: ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2 on Daimon-20 substrate, air incident
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 22 layers
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: ZnS and MgF2 are both conventional evaporatable/sputterable IR dielectrics
Daimon-20 substrate is IR-transparent and thermally stable
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance at design wavelength when optical thickness equals λ/4
Recalled knowledge: Dual-band filters require thickness tuning so multiple interference orders align with both passbands
Recalled knowledge: ZnS has refractive index approximately 2.2-2.4 in the 4-5 μm range with low absorption
Recalled knowledge: MgF2 has refractive index approximately 1.3-1.4 in the 4-5 μm range with low absorption
Recalled knowledge: Index contrast of ~0.8-1.0 between high and low layers provides adequate reflectance per interface for IR filtering
expected_advantages: ZnS/MgF2 pair is well-established for IR coatings from recalled practice
22 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization
Alternating topology is manufacturable with standard deposition equipment
No metal layers avoids absorption losses in the IR
known_risks: Uncertain whether ZnS and MgF2 remain sufficiently transparent at 5.2 μm - may have absorption edges I cannot recall precisely. Would need to check measured k values in the material registry.
Uncertain about exact refractive index dispersion in the 3.6-5.2 μm range - my recalled values are approximate. The solver will read actual measured data.
Uncertain whether 22 layers is optimal vs 20 or 24 - chose 22 as a middle value from recalled practice but this is not verified.
Uncertain about adhesion between ZnS and MgF2 on Daimon-20 - may require adhesion layers not modeled here.
The quarter-wave starting point may not be optimal for dual-band operation; thickness optimization is essential.
Daimon-20 is one of four CaF2 datasets in the registry; I cannot verify from memory whether this specific dataset covers the full 3.6-5.2 μm range needed.
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer planar multilayer infrared filter coating on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees. Use alternating ZnS and MgF2 layers starting with ZnS as layer 1. Optimize individual layer thicknesses with bounds 50-1000 nm per layer. Target high transmittance in two passbands: 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm. Target low transmittance in two stopbands: 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Use coherent thin-film matrix method solver. Evaluate unpolarized light at normal incidence. Maximum 24 layers constraint satisfied with 22 layers. No metal layers used. Materials ZnS and MgF2 are from the guaranteed material catalog. Substrate is CaF2 (Daimon-20).

unresolved_decisions: Whether ZnS/MgF2 is the optimal material pair for this wavelength range vs alternatives like Si/SiO2 or ZnSe/MgF2
Whether 22 layers is the right count vs 20 or 24 for balancing performance and manufacturability
Exact refractive index values and dispersion curves for ZnS and MgF2 in the 3.6-5.2 μm range
Whether Daimon-20 substrate requires any surface treatment for adhesion with these materials
Whether Daimon-20 dataset covers the full 3.6-5.2 μm spectral range needed for this design
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route cannot achieve target_score above 0.6 after three refinement rounds, the fundamental hypothesis that alternating dielectric stacks can achieve this dual-band separation with these materials may be incorrect, and a different topology (such as defect-cavity or chirped stack) should be considered.

expected_observations: If the hypothesis holds, best_target_score should increase across optimization rounds as thicknesses converge toward dual-band alignment
If the hypothesis holds, valid_candidates count should remain stable or increase as the optimizer finds physically valid thickness combinations
If the hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau early below 0.5 indicating the material pair or topology cannot achieve the spectral separation
If the hypothesis fails, tightest_margin will decrease across rounds indicating the design is approaching physical impossibility
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates drops to zero for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 10% and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.1 for three consecutive rounds, reduce layer count to 20 and restart optimization

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
